entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-r8hm-w5f7-wj39: Cross-site scripting vulnerability in TinyMCE plugins
entry.content:
Cross-site scripting vulnerability in TinyMCE plugins

Aliases: CVE-2024-21910, PYSEC-2026-632

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • tinymce — fixed in 5.10.0
  • tinymce/tinymce — fixed in 5.10.0
  • TinyMCE — fixed in 5.10.0
  • django-tinymce — fixed in 3.4.0

### Impact A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in the URL processing logic of the `image` and `link` plugins. The vulnerability allowed arbitrary JavaScript execution when updating an image or link using a specially crafted URL. This issue only impacted users while editing and the dangerous URLs were stripped in any content extracted from the editor. This impacts all users who are using TinyMCE 5.9.2 or lower. ### Patches This vulnerability has been patched in TinyMCE 5.10.0 by improved sanitization logic when updating URLs in the relevant plugins. ### Workarounds To work around this vulnerability, either: - Upgrade to TinyMCE 5.10.0 or higher - Disable the `image` and `link` plugins ### Acknowledgements Tiny Technologies would like to thank Yakir6 for discovering …

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-6c3j-c64m-qhgq: XSS in jQuery as used in Drupal, Backdrop CMS, and other products
entry.content:
XSS in jQuery as used in Drupal, Backdrop CMS, and other products

Aliases: CVE-2019-11358, DRUPAL-CORE-2019-006, PYSEC-2026-628

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • jquery — fixed in 3.4.0
  • jquery-rails — fixed in 4.3.4
  • jQuery — fixed in 3.4.0
  • django — fixed in 2.1.9
  • django — fixed in 2.2.2
  • org.webjars.npm:jquery — fixed in 3.4.0
  • maximebf/debugbar — fixed in 1.19.0

jQuery from 1.1.4 until 3.4.0, as used in Drupal, Backdrop CMS, and other products, mishandles `jQuery.extend(true, {}, ...)` because of `Object.prototype` pollution. If an unsanitized source object contained an enumerable `__proto__` property, it could extend the native `Object.prototype`.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-4j9m-h44m-2hv8: Steeltoe: OAEP setting silently selects PKCS#1 v1.5 padding
entry.content:
Steeltoe: OAEP setting silently selects PKCS#1 v1.5 padding

Aliases: CVE-2026-50268

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • Steeltoe.Configuration.Encryption — fixed in 4.2.0

### Summary Configuring `encrypt:rsa:algorithm=OAEP` does not enable OAEP encryption. Due to an incorrect BouncyCastle transformation string, the `OAEP` setting selects PKCS#1 v1.5, which is the same algorithm as the `DEFAULT` setting. ### Impact Operators who configure `encrypt:rsa:algorithm=OAEP` to obtain CCA2-secure padding receive PKCS#1 v1.5 instead. Currently, `Decrypt()` is called only against operator-controlled configuration data, so no exploitable path exists, but any future code path that exposes a decryption oracle would be Bleichenbacher-vulnerable despite the `OAEP` setting. ### Migration note Existing `{cipher}` values produced under the broken `OAEP` setting were encrypted with PKCS#1 v1.5. The fix makes `OAEP` use actual OAEP padding, so those values will fail to dec…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-227r-jm2g-7cp4: Steeltoe's sensitive actuators (heapdump/env) only require Restricted permission
entry.content:
Steeltoe's sensitive actuators (heapdump/env) only require Restricted permission

Aliases: CVE-2026-50201

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • Steeltoe.Management.Endpoint — fixed in 4.2.0
  • Steeltoe.Management.EndpointBase — fixed in 3.4.0

### Summary All Steeltoe actuator endpoints default to `EndpointPermissions.Restricted`, which is mapped to Cloud Foundry's `read_basic_data` permission (granted to Space Auditors and similar low-trust roles). Sensitive actuators including heap dump, environment, and thread dump do not raise this to `EndpointPermissions.Full`, so CF's `read_sensitive_data` permission flag is not enforced for those endpoints. Spring Boot's equivalent Cloud Foundry integration gates these endpoints with `read_sensitive_data` by default. ### Impact Any CF user holding Space Auditor, Space Manager, or Org Auditor role can access the heap dump, environment, and thread dump actuators for any Steeltoe application in their space. A heap dump contains all in-memory data including database passwords, bearer token…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-7fqc-p256-7pwj: Steeltoe's static JWKS cache shared across schemes and never invalidated
entry.content:
Steeltoe's static JWKS cache shared across schemes and never invalidated

Aliases: CVE-2026-50202

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • Steeltoe.Security.Authentication.JwtBearer — fixed in 4.2.0
  • Steeltoe.Security.Authentication.OpenIdConnect — fixed in 4.2.0
  • Steeltoe.Security.Authentication.CloudFoundryBase — fixed in 3.4.0

### Summary The JWT signing key cache in `TokenKeyResolver` uses `kid` as the sole cache key without namespacing by authority. In applications with multiple `JwtBearer` schemes pointing to different identity providers, a key fetched for one scheme can satisfy token validation for another. Additionally, cached keys have no expiration, so rotated or revoked keys remain trusted until the application process restarts. ### Impact In multi-scheme deployments, an attacker who controls one identity provider's signing key can forge tokens accepted by other schemes within the same application. For all applications using `TokenKeyResolver`, a signing key removed from the identity provider's JWKS endpoint remains trusted indefinitely. ### Mitigations If an immediate upgrade is not possible: - In…

### Summary The `Sanitizer` component in the Environment actuator redacts configuration values by matching the configuration key name against a suffix list. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-24c8-4792-22hx: Scriban: array.insert_at index parameter DoS bypasses LoopLimit and LimitToString
entry.content:
Scriban: array.insert_at index parameter DoS bypasses LoopLimit and LimitToString

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • scriban — fixed in 7.2.0
  • Scriban.Signed — fixed in 7.2.0

## Summary `ArrayFunctions.InsertAt` in Scriban allocates `index - list.Count` null entries in a tight C# `for` loop with no bound on `index`. The function is exposed to template authors as `array.insert_at`, and the fill loop ignores every existing safety control: `LoopLimit`, `LimitToString`, `ObjectRecursionLimit`, and `RecursiveLimit`. A single template such as `{{ [1] | array.insert_at 200000000 'x' | array.size }}` causes `OutOfMemoryException` in well under a second on a host with 1 GB of memory, even when `LoopLimit` is set to `10` and `LimitToString` is set to `100`. Because `OutOfMemoryException` is generally not caught by the template renderer or by typical host applications, the vulnerability terminates the host process, not just the template. This is a sibling vector to GHSA…
